title: Freddie Mercury's birth chart
metaDescription: Freddie Mercury's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 12.2° Virgo. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: Four of the nine placements whose signs are settled stand in Libra — Venus, Mars, Jupiter and Neptune. The placements whose signs could change with an unknown hour are not counted. A cluster that size becomes the section the rest of the chart plays around.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: Virgo, but precisely: 12.2°, second decan, 10°–20°, under Saturn in the triplicity scheme. The tradition kept these divisions because thirty degrees is a long street.

blocks.title: Closer to the ground
blocks.text: Day to day the chart speaks through Mercury in Virgo (3.2°), Venus in Libra (28.4°), Mars in Libra (17.2°): a mind that trusts the measured and the checked, taste led by wit and proportion, drive that argues its way forward.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Venus and Jupiter hold the closest angle here — a conjunction, 2.3° wide. A conjunction concentrates rather than balances — the pair burns one fuel line. Behind it, Saturn sextile Neptune at 3.3°, and Mars trine Uranus at 4.4° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. These are the day-proof angles — present at midnight, present at noon, present at the next midnight.

blocks.title: What the angles build
blocks.text: Pluto stands apart from every major angle the day held — the tradition reads an unaspected planet as a voice that speaks on its own schedule, unmodulated by the rest of the chart.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Of the seven planets the classical scheme judges, four sit in a sign it has an opinion about. Mercury in Virgo at 3.2° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best; Venus in Libra at 28.4° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules; Mars in Libra at 17.2° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain; Saturn in Leo at 4.1° is in detriment. The old table grades terrain, not talent — a placement in fall works uphill, nothing more.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: The honest balance sheet uses the 9 placements whose signs hold for the whole day: air 5, earth 2, fire 2 across the elements, and cardinal 4, mutable 3, fixed 2 across the modalities. No settled placement falls in water — an absence the tradition treats as information, not as a defect. Nothing was retrograde that day, which is less common than it sounds.

blocks.title: The Moon is genuinely open
blocks.text: The Moon crossed from Sagittarius into Capricorn during that day at the birthplace, travelling 11.9° between one midnight and the next. Half the day belongs to each sign, and the split falls at an unrecorded hour — so this page holds the Moon as a genuine unknown.
